text: Shared panel base and colour helpers of the component writer scripts. What: panel_type() returns ComponentPanel , the non-modal PythonQt panel of the Components scripts (Align By Anchor, Build From Recipes, Copy Offsets Between Masters, Decompose, Nested Finder, Replace Reference, Unlock Lock): script controls, a live preview table, Reload selection, Close and Apply. ink , muted and readable_palette give readable text colours in FontLab's light and dark themes. ERROR_COLOR colours blocked rows; MAX_ROWS limits the preview rows. The helpers are the same objects as in fontlabapp.anchors.panel.model and fontlabapp.metrics.panel.model . How: the panel plans with fontlabapp.components.writer ( collect , blocked_rows , require_safe ) on every control change. Apply plans again from live data, scans the auto-layer facts again and writes with component_writer.apply_work and the script's editor() (one Undo step). Signals connect through scripting.connect_guarded and disconnect in closeEvent . Why: each script then holds only its planner, a small panel subclass and main . This module imports only stdlib-only App modules at load time; PythonQt loads inside the functions, and panel_type() loads the class from fontlabapp.components.panel.ui . So FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast, and tests without Qt can import it. Offline tests do not prove native panel behaviour. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.components.panel.model as component_panel import fly.ap.components.writer as component_writer class Decompose(component_panel.panel_type()): TITLE, KEY, ACTION, DONE = "Decompose Components", "components_decompose", "Decompose", "Decomposed" HEADERS = ("Glyph · master", "Component", "Becomes") def build_controls(self): ... def planner(self): ... def editor(self): return component_writer.EjectEditor(unlock=True)

text: capture () -> RecipeSnapshot Capture actual selected layers, including ordered repeated editor slots. Use the shared Font/Glyph-window provider, read all components twice and reject changed observed identities, names, shape order or document context. A single2sdeadline covers every provider/component loop. No current-glyph fallback, sorting, deduplication, font write or partial result is used. Blocking native calls cannot be preempted; native acceptance remains open.

text: recipes ( layers : tuple [ RecipeLayer , ... ]) -> str Return original base+base=glyph lines, without deduplication or sorting. Skip only layers without components. Keep missing-base names literally. A recipe records composition, not exact geometry or guaranteed import into another editor. The original format omits all transforms and offsets. Keep the final newline emitted by the original per-layer print call.

text: Pure 2D affine math in Qt's row-vector convention. No Qt import. What it does: Holds a transform as six floats (a, b, c, d, e, f) , the same order as QTransform(m11, m12, m21, m22, dx, dy) . A point maps as x' = a*x + c*y + e and y' = b*x + d*y + f . How to use: concat(first, then) applies first , then then . This is Qt's first * then . apply maps one point. invert gives the inverse. rotation makes a rotation; IDENTITY changes nothing. from_qtransform copies a native QTransform into plain floats. viewport_transform reads a FontLab canvas map as one Affine. Example: apply(concat(glyph_to_canvas, canvas_to_view), x, y) maps one glyph point to widget pixels. Why this design: - Plain tuples keep no native wrapper alive and are safe in paint code. - No Qt import. The module loads in a cold FontLab start (5 s limit) and in tests without PythonQt. Qt classes arrive as arguments. - Every public function rejects non-finite numbers with ValueError by default. A bad native matrix then fails loud, not as a silent bad paint. Pass finite=False only for deliberate raw math. Used by: canvas_rsb , canvas_anchor_rings , drawing . Glyport adopts the same names later ( fontlab_glyport.drawing.context ).

text: Contour copies and Qt path contours of the Contours generator scripts. What: Shadow Copy, Small Caps From Capitals, Superior & Inferior Figures and Tabular Figure Copies copy the contours of a layer through a transform; Outline Effect turns a stroked QPainterPath back into FontLab contours. This module holds those shared parts: contour_shapes gives the own (non-component) shapes that hold contours. copy_contours copies their contours: first the element transform, then the caller's transform. repair_nodes copies the node names and raw node flags back onto each copy. path_contours builds closed flContour objects from the elements of a QPainterPath . How: a contour copy is contour.cloneMapped(...) . FontLab's contour copy can drop node names and raw node flags (fl#8569). repair_nodes copies only these two fields back: the node names and raw node flags. Other node properties, contour names and element names and notes are not copied by copy_contours . restore_shape repairs a whole detached shape, including its shape-data name/note and contour names. It keeps clone selection bits by default; keep_view_state=True restores source selection and active flags. Why: the code was a private copy in five scripts. contour_shapes is not fontlabapp.contours.writer.outline_shapes : that one returns the shapes that an outline script may edit in place, and it keeps shared and scaled shapes out. A copy can use those shapes too, because it maps every contour through its element transform. This module imports only the standard library at load time. path_contours loads fontlab and PythonQt when it runs, so FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast. Offline tests do not prove native FontLab behaviour. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.contours.copy as contour_copy copies = contour_copy.copy_contours(layer, move) # read before history

text: Measure the vertical extent of a layer from its outline nodes. What: vertical_extent(layer) returns (ymin, ymax) of every contour of every shape of layer , or None when no contour has a node. Why: FontLab keeps flLayer.boundingBox and flShape.boundingBox as a cache. After a Python node move, the cache stays stale, also after notifyChangesApplied (fl#8575, FontLab 9.0.9790). This module never reads a boundingBox and never calls update() , so the read has no side effects. How: each shape's contours are mapped through shape.transform (an affine QTransform, read through m11() … m33() ), so a component counts at its placement, as in masters.layer_contours . Shapes without contours (stickers, empty shapes) give nothing. Nodes come from contour.nodes() as node.x , node.y and their kind: node.isOn() (on-curve), node.isCurve() (cubic control, flNode::Curve ) or else a quadratic control ( flNode::Off , node.isOff() ; flnode.h). The kind decides each segment, not contour.isTT : FontLab sets isTT when any node is a quadratic control, so one contour can mix both kinds (flcontour.cpp). As in FontLab's contour enumerator (flconturenum.h), an implied on-curve midpoint lies only between two consecutive Off nodes. Each segment between two on-curve nodes gives its end y values and its exact y extremes: the roots of the cubic derivative in (0, 1) for two Curve controls, or the one extreme for one Off control. A closed contour also gives its closing segment. Not counted, by design: stroke thickness ( maxThickness , which flShape.boundingBox adds), because zones measure the outline; and the per-contour contour.transform() , which is identity outside an interactive transform (flshapedata.cpp).

text: Shared plan kernel of the outline writer scripts (Contours folder). What: the Contours writer scripts (Round Coordinates, Remove Overlap, Add Extremes, Correct Contour Direction, Straighten Short Curves, Optimize Start Points, Delete Small Contours, Fix Zero Handles, Delete Duplicate Contours, Transform, Slant) share one model. A script planner turns one layer into Change rows; the script's Editor writes them through apply_work (one Undo step). This module adds the outline parts to the generic fontlabapp.masters.layers.writer kernel and re-exports that kernel: outline_shapes gives the own contour shapes that a script may edit in place, and a note for every shape that it keeps (shared outline data, scaled or rotated shapes). note_rows turns the notes into rows. node_points and translation read nodes and plain shape moves. collect runs the planner on every chosen layer. A glyph that the geometry policy refuses is listed and skipped as a whole; the other glyphs are still written. With compatible , a glyph whose structure edits would differ between masters is held back ( held_back ). require_safe is a compatibility hook; apply_work discloses queued glyph updates through history (FontLab issue 8537). How: a Change.key names a structure edit (for example the index of a deleted contour). held_back compares the keys of all masters: the masters stay compatible only when every master gets the same keys and every master with a key edit is in scope. Why: the logic was a private copy in each of the eleven scripts. The refusal policy differs from component_writer on purpose: an outline batch skips each refused glyph, with a row that says why, and asks for consent ( allow_bases ) before it edits bases of automatic composites. This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules ( history , edit_guards , layer_writer ) at load time, so FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast. The panel base is in fontlabapp.contours.panel.model . Offline tests do not prove native Undo/Redo. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.contours.writer as outline_writer def planner(glyph, master, layer): shapes, notes = outline_writer.outline_shapes(layer) rows = [outline_writer.Change("nodes", "3", "4", ("nodes", shapes))] return rows + outline_writer.note_rows(notes) plan = outline_writer.collect(glyphs, masters, planner, facts) outline_writer.require_safe() outline_writer.apply_work(plan.work, "Example", facts, ExampleEditor())
title: fontlabapp.contours.writer

text: Shared panel base and colour helpers of the outline writer scripts. What: panel_type() returns OutlinePanel , the non-modal PythonQt panel of the Contours writer scripts: script controls, the master scope, a "Keep masters compatible" tick for scripts that change the node structure, a consent tick for bases of automatic composites, a live preview table, Reload selection, Close and Apply. ink , muted and readable_palette give readable text colours in FontLab's light and dark themes. ERROR_COLOR colours blocked rows; MAX_ROWS limits the preview rows. The helpers are the same objects as in fontlabapp.anchors.panel.model . How: the panel plans with fontlabapp.contours.writer.collect on every control change. Apply plans again from live data, scans the auto-layer facts again and writes with outline_writer.apply_work and the script's editor() (one Undo step). A new scan clears the consent tick, because the consent belongs to the glyphs that the user saw. Signals connect through scripting.connect_guarded and disconnect in closeEvent . Why: each script then holds only its own logic, a small panel subclass and main . OutlinePanel is its own class, not a subclass of fontlabapp.components.panel.model 's ComponentPanel : the scope, the ticks, the per-glyph refusal, the error display of Apply and the status texts differ, so a subclass would replace almost every method. This module imports only stdlib-only App modules at load time; PythonQt loads inside the functions, and panel_type() loads the class from fontlabapp.contours.panel.ui . So FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast, and tests without Qt can import it. Offline tests do not prove native panel behaviour. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.contours.panel.model as outline_panel import fly.ap.contours.writer as outline_writer class RoundCoordinates(outline_panel.panel_type()): TITLE, KEY, ACTION, DONE, UNIT = "Round Coordinates", "outlines_round", "Round", "Rounded", "item" def build_controls(self): ... def planner(self): ... def editor(self): ...

text: panel_type () -> type Return the OutlinePanel base class (a PythonQt QDialog ). The class loads PythonQt, so call this inside FontLab only. Subclass it, set TITLE , KEY , ACTION , DONE , UNIT , HEADERS (3 or 4 columns) and STRUCTURAL (True when the edits change node counts or order), and fill in the hooks build_controls , planner and editor ; optionally build_extra , on_reload and after_refresh (all in HOOKS ). spin(...) makes a watched spin box. MEMBERS lists the other public members a script may use, for example slot_error , status and apply_button . See fontlabapp.contours.panel.ui.OutlinePanel for the full contract. Show it with scripting.show_script_dialog(Subclass, Subclass.KEY) .

Subclasses set TITLE, KEY, ACTION, DONE, UNIT, HEADERS and STRUCTURAL, and override build_controls(), planner() and editor(). The preview recomputes on every control change and shows exactly what Apply would write. Apply stays off while any row is blocked.

text: Shared panel base of the Contours scripts that work on the selected glyphs. What: panel_type() returns SelectionPanel , the non-modal PythonQt panel of Shadow Copy, Outline Effect, Autohint Selected Layers and Remove PostScript Hints: script controls, a master scope ("Current master" or "All masters"), a consent tick for bases of automatic composites ( BASES_TEXT ), a preview table, a status line and the buttons Use selection, Close and the action. fontlabapp.glyphs.copies.panel_type() returns CopiesPanel , the same base set up for the scripts that create glyph copies. How: the panel binds to the font that is current when it opens and takes the Font window selection. The public facts attribute stores auto-layer facts from construction, reselect() or scan() (explicit Refresh). Use self.facts in plan_rows to avoid a whole-font scan for each control signal. Every control change plans again with the script's plan_rows and fills the table with its cells . The action plans again from the live font and calls the script's write once. Use selection reads the selection again and clears the consent tick, because the consent belongs to the glyphs that the user saw. A refusal ( ValueError , RuntimeError or TimeoutError ) in Use selection or in the action shows its text in the status line. Signals connect through scripting.connect_guarded and disconnect when the panel closes. Why: the four panels differed only in their controls, so each script now holds only its own logic, a small panel subclass and main . The panel is not fontlabapp.contours.panel.model 's OutlinePanel : that one plans outline_writer rows; these scripts plan their own rows. MAX_ROWS is the fontlabapp.anchors.panel.model limit. This module imports only stdlib-only App modules at load time; panel_type() loads the class from fontlabapp.contours.selection.panel.ui , which imports PythonQt. Offline tests do not prove native panel behaviour. text: Shared transform writer and preview of Contours > Transform and Slant. What: both scripts apply one affine matrix to the chosen layers. transform_changes plans one layer: one row for its shapes and one row for its anchors. TransformEditor writes the plan; bakes decides per shape how. layer_outline , mapped , outline_path and fit feed the before/after preview. panel_type() returns TransformPanel : the OutlinePanel of fontlabapp.contours.panel.model plus an outline preview of the first glyph that may change. How: every shape gets the composed transform (old shape transform, then the matrix). A shape that bakes accepts then gets shape.applyTransform() : FontLab writes the new nodes and resets the matrix. This is FontLab's own per-shape rule of the layer transform ( fllayer.cpp:6957-6978 ): it bakes only own contour shapes that only move, whose data no other shape shares and that include no other shapes, and composes every other shape. The write never calls layer.applyTransform : the one-argument Python binding also moves the guides, scales the advance and moves every anchor. Anchors move in place, only when the user asks. An existing anchor that would land on 0, 0 blocks Apply: anchor_writer.on_origin is the shared Redo rule (FontLab issue 8527), here with a tolerance of ORIGIN_NEAR because FontLab may round the stored point. The read-back accepts the same tolerance for rounded nodes and anchors. Why: Transform and Slant used private copies of this code. This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules ( affine , anchor_writer , outline_writer ) at load time. PythonQt loads inside the functions, and panel_type() loads the class from fontlabapp.contours.transform.ui , so FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast. Offline tests do not prove native Undo/Redo. How to use (a script):: import fly.ap.contours.transform.model as outline_transform class Slant(outline_transform.panel_type()): def preview_matrix(self, layer): return matrix, guide_y def planner(self): return lambda glyph, master, layer: outline_transform.transform_changes( layer, matrix, True, "250" ) def editor(self): return outline_transform.TransformEditor()

text: bakes ( shape : Any ) -> bool True when FontLab's own layer transform writes the new nodes into the shape. FontLab's rule ( fllayer.cpp:6957-6978 ): an own contour shape whose transform only moves, whose outline data no other shape shares and that includes no other shapes gets new node positions. Every other shape (components, shared data, scaled shapes) keeps its nodes and gets the composed shape transform. This function follows that rule and also composes a shape with no contours, which FontLab would bake. That is harmless: such a shape has no nodes to write.

text: transform_changes ( layer : Any , matrix : Affine , anchors : bool , note : str ) -> list [ Change ] Rows for one layer: the shapes, then the anchors when asked. Shape edit: ("shapes", [(shape, new shape transform, bakes, probe)]); probe is (first node, its expected glyph position) for a baked shape. Anchor edit: ("anchors", [(anchor, x, y)]). An anchor that would move onto 0, 0 blocks Apply: FontLab cannot redo that move (fl#8527). The rule is anchor_writer.on_origin : the new point counts with the ORIGIN_NEAR rounding tolerance, the old point only when it is exactly 0, 0. So an anchor at (0.3, 0) that moves to (0, 0) is refused; only an anchor that is exactly on the origin already does not count.

text: Public queue disclosure and refusal guards for scripts that write to the current font. What: queue disclosure for ordinary writers, and four checks that raise ValueError before any native write. require_selection_window(package_id) : the active panel is a Font window of the bound font (FontLab issue 8528: selection writers crash while a Glyph window is active). require_no_editors() : no Glyph editor is open, also an inactive one (the Unicode save-cache gap of the duplicate-Unicode writer). require_settled() : FontLab has no queued native glyph updates (FontLab issue 8537: queued cache updates become semantic edits later). require_history_scope(glyphs, creates=...) : no Glyph window is the active canvas, or every owner glyph is in that canvas and no glyph is new (FontLab issue 8573: from a Glyph window, the Undo step covers only the glyphs that the canvas shows). fontlabapp.core.history.glyphs.commit , fontlabapp.glyphs.creation.create_glyphs and the eight App writers that call notifyChangesApplied directly call it. How: the selection and editor guards delegate to the reviewed private implementation ( scripting._require_selection_window , duplicate_unicodes_capture.require_no_editors ); require_settled reads the native queue once; require_history_scope reads the text blocks of the active canvas once. The implementations load only when a guard runs, so this module imports only the standard library and FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast. Why: scripts must not import private App names. Use these guards through fly.ap.core.edit_guards . fontlabapp.core.history.glyphs.commit discloses the queue by default; settled=True explicitly opts into refusing it. Never normalise unrelated dates. Offline tests do not prove native behaviour.
title: fontlabapp.core.edit_guards

text: Native outline reads that studios may not reach directly. What: merged_copy(shape) returns a detached FontGate copy of a native flShape with its overlaps removed (the Scriptmix Remove Overlap route: convertToFgShape then fgShape.removeOverlap ), and font_info returns fontpr's get_font_info JSON for a package, which carries every master's metrics and stems without switching the current master. Why: the studio boundary refuses fontgate and fontlabapp._native ; the Outline Doctor ( fontlabapp.studios.outline_doctor ) calls these. Neither function writes the font. Only convertToFgShape , removeOverlap and the copy's contours / countNodes are touched: probing other FontGate attributes has crashed the host (AGENTS.md, Issue 235).

text: canvas_glyphs ( native : Any = None , * , deadline : float | None = None ) -> frozenset [ tuple [ int , str ]] | None Return the glyphs that the active Glyph window shows, or None . None : no Glyph window is the active canvas, so FontLab records package history. Otherwise return one (package id, glyph name) pair for each glyph in the text blocks of the active canvas. Use the name, not the id: CurrentGlyph().id and the canvas slot id of the same glyph differ on 9790 (412 against 531175085312). These are the glyphs that FontLab's canvas history attaches an Undo step to ( flhistorycontroller.cpp , the in_glyphs branch; FontLab issue 8573). Empty slots are skipped. deadline is a time.monotonic() instant (default: now plus CANVAS_SCAN_SECONDS ); a later checkpoint raises TimeoutError . Native read errors propagate. A fontlab module without flWorkspace , or a workspace without getActiveCanvas (offline doubles), has no canvas: return None . FontLab's own module always defines both.

text: require_history_scope ( glyphs : Sequence [ Any ], * , creates : bool = False , native : Any = None ) -> None Refuse a write that FontLab would undo only in part (FontLab issue 8573). While a Glyph window is the active canvas, FontLab attaches the Undo step of notifyChangesApplied only to the glyphs that this canvas shows. Other notified glyphs keep the change after Undo (measured on 9790). With the Font window active, the Undo step covers every notified glyph. glyphs : the owner glyphs of the write, matched by font and glyph name. creates : the write makes new glyphs (a new glyph is never in the canvas). Raise ValueError(CANVAS_TEXT) before any write when a Glyph window is the active canvas and the write creates glyphs, or when an owner is not in the canvas. When the canvas cannot be read, use the safe rule: allow no owner, or one owner that is the current glyph, and no new glyph. With no active canvas, return. Call it on the GUI thread only; other threads are refused. native is the fontlab module (default: the native one).
title: fontlabapp.core.edit_guards.require_history_scope

text: require_no_editors ( * , qt : Any = None , deadline : float | None = None , action : str = 'removing Unicode assignments' ) -> None Refuse a write while any Glyph editor is open, also an inactive one. qt is the PythonQt module (default: the native one). deadline is a time.monotonic() instant (default: now plus EDITOR_SCAN_SECONDS ). action completes the refusal text "before ." Raise ValueError for an open or unreadable editor and TimeoutError when the widget scan passes the deadline. The scan reads only the inherits("GlyphWindow") predicate, with cyclic GC off.

text: One native Undo step for a script edit, with auto-layer refusals. What: commit runs a script's font change as ONE FontLab Undo step, in the order that the reviewed App writers use: Refuse before any write ( ValueError , nothing touched): queued native glyph updates only with settled=True (FontLab issue 8537; otherwise disclose them); optionally a missing Font window or an open Glyph editor (Unicode writers); a Glyph window as the active canvas when an owner glyph is not in that canvas (FontLab issue 8573: the Undo step would cover only the shown glyphs; see edit_guards.require_history_scope ); an auto layer in the edit list or among the retained objects; a glyph that the operation policy refuses. checkInitHistoryState(0) on every layer, then every glyph. mutate() . It may return the new native objects it made (for example new layers); they join the notification after the declared layers. One shared UTC lastModified stamp on every glyph. ONE notifyChangesApplied(title, layers + created + glyphs) . With retained objects: ONE notifyChangesApplied(title, retain + layers + created + glyphs, True) . The same stamp again: window observers re-stamp after the history capture. read_back() : the caller compares the font with its plan. Retained objects ( retain= ): a script that removes a component gives the ORIGINAL shape, its shapeData and the builder, read BEFORE the removal ( component_history(shape) ). They go first in the notification, before the layers, and the third argument True asks for deep history. Glyport does the same ( fontlab_backend._retain_component_history and _notify ): its docstring says FontLab 9784 needs this to restore a removed component on Undo (fl#7641). Without retain the call is the two-argument call, unchanged. Steps 4 to 6 run also after a failed mutate , so a partial edit stays on the Undo stack. Every failure is collected and raised as PartialWriteError (a RuntimeError ) whose text says "Native changes may remain; use Edit > Undo". No rollback is tried: Edit > Undo is the recovery. Why the refusals: notifying a list that holds an auto layer makes FontLab re-resolve every default-recipe auto layer in the font, and a change to a base glyph rebuilds its auto composites. Anchors and locks can change and Undo does not restore them (measured; see the workspace AGENTS.md). The policy depends on the operation: "rename" , "unicode" , "geometry" : refuse glyphs that own an auto layer and glyphs that are a base of an auto composite (also through a chain of manual composites). allow_bases=True lets a base through after the user agreed to the rebuild; an auto owner is never let through. "metadata" (notes, tags, mark colours): refuse only glyphs that own an auto layer. How to use:: import fly.ap.core.history.glyphs as history facts = history.scan_auto_facts(package) result = history.commit( "Round Advances", layers, glyphs, lambda: edit(layers), operation="geometry", facts=facts, read_back=check, ) report(result.mismatches) The module imports only the standard library at load time; FontLab modules and fontlabapp.guides.inspect.model load when a function runs. Offline tests prove the call order only, not native Undo/Redo/reopen behaviour.

text: One native Undo step for font-level edits on one or more masters. What: commit_masters writes master values (zones, vertical metrics) as ONE FontLab Undo step. It uses route A of the issue 122 M2 measurement (FontLab 9.0.9790): the history objects of Font Info and "Sync font metrics" ( dlgfontinfo.cpp:2100-2175 , mainwindow_edit.cpp:1208-1226 ): Refuse before any native write ( ValueError ): a thread other than the GUI thread; no active Font window of this font, or a Glyph window as the active canvas (measured in the Font window only); an unknown, duplicate or empty master list; an empty title. Read the queued glyph ids once ( edit_guards.pending_updates ). Never clear them. checkInitHistoryState(0) on the package and on ONE package.mastersContainer() handle. For each requested master, in font order: setMaster(name, False) , read() and save() (the values to restore), write() , read() again and verify() that value. setMaster(original, False) . ONE flItems().notifyChangesApplied(title, [package, container], False) . No glyph and no layer is in the list, so no auto layer is notified. Rollback policy (a decision that differs from history.commit ): history.commit always notifies, also after a failure, and Edit > Undo is the recovery. Here a failure in steps 3 to 5 (a write callback error, or a read-back mismatch) comes BEFORE the notification. So the helper restores every master that it touched, in reverse order, reads each one back, and notifies nothing. Edit > Undo would revert the user's previous step, so no error text recommends it. An interrupt ( KeyboardInterrupt , SystemExit ) also runs the rollback and the master restore, then is raised unchanged. All values restored: raise RolledBackError (a ValueError : the font is as before, like a refusal). A caller whose restore re-creates native objects passes restored_text to say so ( zone_native ). A restore failed, or the notification failed: raise UnrestoredError (a history.PartialWriteError ). Values can remain with no Undo step. Known host defect (fl#8574, measured on 9.0.9790, issue 122 M2): after Edit > Undo or Redo of such a step, both masters show only 3 of the 9 font-metric guidelines (the zone guidelines) until package.updateFontMetrics() runs or the font is reopened. The saved file is correct. This module does not patch Undo; it cannot hook the user's Undo. How to use:: import fly.ap.core.history.masters as font_history edit = font_history.MasterEdit(save, write, read, verify, restore) result = font_history.commit_masters(package, "Edit Zones", {"Bold": edit}) edit_guards.disclose(result) The module imports only the standard library at load time. Offline tests prove the call order only, not native Undo/Redo/reopen behaviour.

text: commit ( title : str , layers : Sequence [ Any ], glyphs : Sequence [ Any ], mutate : Callable [[], Iterable [ Any ] | None ], * , operation : Operation , facts : AutoFacts , allow_bases : bool = False , read_back : Callable [[], Iterable [ str ]] | None = None , settled : bool = False , window : int | None = None , native : Any = None , stamp : Any = None , retain : Sequence [ Any ] = (), glyph_window_ok : bool = False ) -> Committed Run mutate as ONE native Undo step. See the module text for the order. title : the Undo name. layers : every existing layer that mutate changes (all layers of a glyph for renames and Unicode). glyphs : their owner glyphs. mutate() : the edit; return new native objects to notify, or None . operation and facts : the refusal policy ( facts from a fresh scan_auto_facts ). allow_bases : let bases of auto composites through after the user agreed. read_back() : return one text per mismatch between font and plan. settled : refuse queued native updates (explicit opt-in; default False discloses pre-write ids in Committed.pending_updates without clearing them). window : the bound package id; when given, run require_selection_window and require_no_editors first (Unicode writers). native / stamp : the fontlab module and the UTC stamp; the defaults are the native module and QDateTime.currentDateTimeUtc() . retain : native objects to keep in the Undo state, first in the list, with the deep-history flag True (use component_history for each removed component, read before the removal). They get no checkInitHistoryState and are not in Committed.created . Empty: the two-argument notification, as before. glyph_window_ok : skip the Glyph-window check ( edit_guards.require_history_scope ). Use it only for a caller that a native test proves safe; no caller uses it now. Raise ValueError before any history call for a refusal. Raise PartialWriteError when anything fails after history started, including a new auto layer from mutate (it stays out of the notification).
title: fontlabapp.core.history.glyphs.commit

text: component_history ( shape : Any ) -> tuple [ Any , ... ] Return the native objects to retain when a script removes shape . What: (shape, shape.shapeData, shapeData.builder) for a component; () for any other shape, so the result can always go to commit(..., retain=...) . Same logic as glyport's _retain_component_history . When: call it BEFORE removeShape , outside mutate . Glyport records that a builder read after detachment can already be too late (fl#7641). A component without shapeData raises ValueError : nothing to retain is a fault, not an empty result. The builder is returned as FontLab gives it.

text: launch ( path : str | Path ) -> dict [ str , Any ] Run a relocated script beside its resources and retain its globals. Ordinary scripts run as main . Rescued ports use build(qt) with the preserved part1 host/ownership helpers; their live handle is returned under rescued_handle and reused until closed. No QApplication is created. Retained GetGo entries bind their original examples namespace explicitly; an already loaded foreign namespace is refused before executing the entry. Only cwd and sys.path are restored; script effects and exceptions propagate.

text: font_id ( package : Any ) -> int Return the font_id that FontLab's fontpr tools need for package . What: int(package.fgId) , the FontGate id of the package. Why: fontpr finds a font by its FontGate id ( MCPTools::findPackage -> flWorkspace::findPackageId compares fgId , source mcptools.cpp:1025-1035 , flworkspace.cpp:1278-1287 ), and get_fonts reports that id. package.id is a different id (the flObject id). With package.id a tool fails with "Font id not found", or, when the ids collide, reads or writes ANOTHER open font. Use: fontpr.call("get_font_info", font_id=scripting.font_id(package)) . text: safe_name ( name : str ) -> bool Return whether a glyph name can appear unescaped in generated FEA. Permit ASCII letters/underscore initially and letters, digits, dots or hyphens thereafter, plus .notdef. This is intentionally conservative: it does not parse escaped FEA names or verify a glyph exists in a font.

text: suffix_pairs ( names : Iterable [ str ], suffix : str ) -> list [ tuple [ str , str ]] Return unique existing base/alternate pairs in alternate-name order. Ignore leading suffix dots, orphan alternates and unsafe names. Every generated pair needs both names in the supplied glyph-name iterable. Empty suffixes yield no pairs. No font or feature source is modified.

text: Generate seeded contextual alternate feature source for the current font. What: Build random context classes and substitution lookups from user-supplied base/alternate rows. Keep the seed to reproduce exactly the same source. How: Read the current glyph catalogue. Assign category members to nonempty classes, then choose a target and context for each rule using a local RNG. Why: OpenType contextual substitutions are deterministic. Random generation makes varied rules; it does not make the shaping engine choose randomly. The native Features editor accepts source, but does not generate seeded contexts. Use: Open a font, enter one base and its alternates per line, adjust counts, categories and seed, then Preview. Copy feature sends the complete generated source to the clipboard. Write feature replaces the code for the previewed feature tag only after Replace existing feature is ticked for a differing block. Preview shows existing and generated code side by side. Adding a tag or writing identical code needs no confirmation. Changing input or refreshing resets the tick. The shared source-bound writer preserves other features and the prefix stay unchanged. Each changing write is recorded as one Undo step. Compile and test in FontLab's Features panel after writing. Benefit: Review and reproduce varied alternates without manual rule entry. The non-modal panel shows the exact block that Write feature stores. The category filter uses Unicode general categories, with base-name inheritance for suffix glyphs; unencoded names without an encoded base match only All. Export flags are not used. Classes stay inside the generated feature block. Independent behaviour rewrite after Alex Slobzheninov, Glyphs-Scripts/Features/Generate Random Alternates Feature.py, Apache-2.0. Repository: https://github.com/slobzheninov/Glyphs-Scripts . No code copied.

text: Edit Qalmi Nastaliq connections and save reverse substitutions in the font. What: Choose a left medial/final glyph, a right medial/initial family and its numbered alternate. Preview entry/exit alignment on any master. Previous and Next step through actual alternates, including s/sd forms. How: Save connection writes a named lookup inside rlig through Fontport's exact-source writer. A JSON comment in that lookup stores the choices, so reopening the tool restores them. Each save is recorded as one Undo step. Existing rlig statements and all other feature blocks stay in place. Earlier unmanaged reverse rules are listed as a warning because they can run first. Saved pairs with missing glyphs appear as named kept rows and produce no rules; their records stay in the font until Drop stale pairs on Save is ticked. Why: FontLab's Features panel edits source text. This panel adds Qalmi pair selection, aligned outlines and grouped reverse contextual substitutions. Use: Open a Qalmi-named font. Choose a pair and alternate, inspect the preview, then Save connection. Compile and test the feature in FontLab's Features panel. Reload reads saved choices. Closing without Save does not change that pair. Benefit: Review and persist connections without editing feature syntax. Credit: Independent behaviour-only rewrite of Simon Cozens, GlyphsScripts/Nastaliq Connection Editor.py, MIT, copyright 2017. Repository: https://github.com/simoncozens/GlyphsScripts . No source code copied.

text: Insert pasted names into the current font's order and save a FontLab encoding. Select a glyph, run the tool, and paste space-separated glyph names. Preview moves known names before the selected glyph, keeping pasted order and removing repetitions. Unknown names are listed. The insertion position stays defined even when the selected glyph is among the pasted names. Save a new .enc file anywhere, then use File > Import > Encoding. Choose the encoding in the Font window; use the encoding chooser's Refresh button as needed. This produces an ordered Encoding view; it does not change the font's stored glyph indices. FontLab's File > Export > Encoding saves a visible order; this tool adds insertion by pasted names. Existing files are kept. No font edit or Undo step is made. The preview shows up to 200 rows; the file contains every supported glyph. Non-ASCII or unsafe glyph names get named kept rows and stay out of the file. Why: Glyphs glyphOrder has no bound FontLab glyph-reorder API. An encoding provides a persistent order that FontLab can import without changing glyph indices. Benefit: Move a pasted sequence in one action and reuse its order in FontLab. Independent behaviour rewrite after Alex Slobzheninov, Glyphs-Scripts, Font Info/glyphOrder - Paste.py, Apache-2.0. Repository: https://github.com/slobzheninov/Glyphs-Scripts . No upstream code, private identifiers or comments are used.

text: Report OS/2 range bits and complete printable codepage coverage from every glyph encoding; no font changes. What it does: Open with a font active. Inspect coverage rows and use Refresh report after encoding changes; review multibyte codepages separately. Benefit: Gather evidence for export-flag decisions without changing font metadata or encodings.

text: Edit family, style, credits and version naming for the current font. What it does: Family, designer, copyright and version name are font-wide; the style name belongs to the current master (FontLab stores it per master). A table previews the changed fields before Apply. Open with a font active. Edit the fields, review the table, then choose Apply. Blank family or style names and invalid version text disable Apply. The undoable edit leaves outlines and other masters' style names intact. Reopen after changing the active master or font so the displayed style scope stays explicit. How it works: Validate all single-line naming fields and stage explicit font-wide or current-master metadata changes. Apply through the shared Font Info history writer. Why this design: Style is master-specific while family and credit fields are global, so the preview must keep their scopes distinct. How to use: Run Font Info > Names and Credits. Edit the fields, review the changed- field table and press Apply. Reopen after changing font or master before editing that master's style. Benefit: Update related naming and credit metadata together while retaining outlines and other masters' style names.

text: Make prefixed trial copies of static fonts exported from the current font. What: Keep selected FontLab glyphs in each matching exported OTF or TTF. Keep .notdef and component dependencies. Ligature expansion is off by default; tick Also keep ligatures to include the extra glyphs listed in the preview. Keep kerning and positioning unless Remove kerning and positioning is ticked. Keep the existing liga substitutions that survive this keep set. Prefix family, full, unique and PostScript names, including CFF names. Preserve copyright and licence records. How: Read exported binaries with fontTools, subset detached copies and save new files. Inspect the saved copies by reopening them in FontLab. No source font or source binary is edited. There is no font edit and no Undo step. Why: File > Export Font As produces the source binaries. This panel adds a selected glyph keep set and consistent trial names across those static exports. It avoids changing a live font or relying on Glyphs export-only custom parameters. Usage: Export static OTF/TTF instances to a folder first. Select the trial glyphs in FontLab. Open this panel, enter that folder, a different output folder and a prefix. Inspect the per-file preview, then press Make Trial Copies. Use selection reads the glyph selection again. Family name and UPM must match the current font; other files get named kept rows. Existing destinations are kept. Variable fonts are kept: export static instances before using this tool. Benefit: Repeatable trial binaries without deleting work from the design source. The keep set uses exported glyph names. Preserve glyph names in the export profile; renamed or absent glyphs are reported instead of silently dropped. Substitution features are limited to liga and the retained positioning feature tags; ligatures are not invented. Requires user-installed fontTools in FontLab's Python site-packages, such as the dependency installed with fontlab-fontport. FontLab's private copy is not used. Install it through Settings > Python if it is missing. Source inspection is cached until the folder or selection changes, or Refresh Exports is pressed. Prefix edits update destination names without opening fonts. Independent behaviour rewrite of Fernando Díaz / Reset Type Studio, Glyphs-Scripts/Exports/Trial Font Maker.py. https://github.com/Reset-Type-Studio/Glyphs-Scripts Apache-2.0, declared in the repository README; no separate LICENSE file. No source code was copied.

text: Bump the numeric version and version name; optionally append a dated font note. What it does: Open with a font active. Choose a major or minor bump and optional dated notes, review the field changes, then choose Apply. Minor 999 carries into the major. Version fields are global; notes are appended to each master's existing note. The edit is undoable. Reopen the panel after switching fonts. How it works: Plan a bounded numeric version and matching version name. Optionally append a dated note to every master's existing note; keep the fields staged until Apply. Why this design: Version naming and numeric metadata must agree, while an optional history note must not replace existing master notes. How to use: Run Font Info > Bump Font Version. Choose major or minor and the dated- note option, inspect all proposed changes and press Apply once for the intended increment. Benefit: Update related version metadata together and retain the previous note content.
